theses.name: AI power bottleneck beneficiaries
theses.summary: AI compute demand is pulling electricity, nuclear, uranium, and grid names into a tradable scarcity narrative.
theses.variant_perception: The market still underestimates how long grid, generation, and fuel constraints can persist.
theses.falsifier: Utility capex or power prices fail to accelerate despite sustained compute demand.

theses.name: AI software and developer tooling watchlist
theses.summary: Developer tooling and AI-app bookmarks may reveal private-market direction but need tradable public proxies.
theses.variant_perception: Private-market excitement is easier to identify than a clean, attractively priced public expression.
theses.falsifier: A public proxy shows durable monetization with falling inference costs.

theses.name: Neocloud and GPU compute burst basket
theses.summary: Bookmarks point to high-beta AI infrastructure names that can move quickly on capacity, financing, and earnings narratives.
theses.variant_perception: Capacity scarcity can outweigh financing anxiety during confirmed demand bursts.
theses.falsifier: Utilization, contracted backlog, or financing access deteriorates materially.

theses.name: AI semiconductor and photonics second derivative
theses.summary: AI capex may spill into networking, optical, memory, and ASIC suppliers beyond the obvious GPU leaders.
theses.variant_perception: Networking and optical suppliers may capture the second derivative of AI capex.
theses.falsifier: 800G/1.6T demand or supplier guidance rolls over across multiple quarters.

theses.name: Biotech royalty asymmetric setup
theses.summary: A bookmarked biotech royalty idea may offer asymmetric upside, but needs specialized evidence before sizing.
theses.variant_perception: The payoff can be asymmetric, but the evidence is too specialized for broad basket exposure.
theses.falsifier: A validated catalyst and independently checked royalty economics emerge.

theses.name: Defense, drones, and space momentum basket
theses.summary: Defense autonomy and space infrastructure names show bookmark momentum and may respond to contract/catalyst headlines.
theses.variant_perception: Procurement is shifting toward cheaper autonomous systems faster than consensus models imply.
theses.falsifier: Contract conversion and production scale continue to lag narrative momentum.

theses.name: Crypto and decentralized AI optionality
theses.summary: Crypto bookmarks suggest lottery-ticket optionality; evidence must be separated from ideology.
theses.variant_perception: Optionality is real, but conviction should stay separate from ideology and liquidity beta.
theses.falsifier: Network usage grows independently of token price and risk appetite.

theses.name: Quantum momentum burst basket
theses.summary: Quantum names are more momentum/speculation than fundamentals, requiring tighter sizing and faster invalidation.
theses.variant_perception: Price action is running ahead of commercially measurable progress.
theses.falsifier: Bookings and technical milestones begin compounding faster than dilution.

predictions.statement: Neocloud public comps experience a material volatility expansion around the Nscale filing or roadshow window.
AI power and grid beneficiaries outperform broad software AI proxies into the next capex-guidance cycle.
The quantum basket underperforms the AI infrastructure basket when momentum cools.
At least two optical-networking suppliers raise forward demand commentary before year-end.

insights.title: IREN is a breaker signal for the neocloud basket
insights.summary: IREN reported revenue stepping down from $240.3M to $184.7M to $144.8M while operating losses widened from $76.4M to $233.5M across the available quarters. Before adding exposure, separate AI-cloud economics from legacy mining mix and validate segment-level demand.

insights.title: Fuel-cycle cash flow deserves a separate sleeve
insights.summary: LEU's latest quarter showed $176.1M of revenue and $10.4M of operating income versus OKLO's $1.2M of revenue and $73.2M operating loss. Nuclear fuel exposure and reactor-development optionality should not share one confidence score or sizing rule.

insights.title: Photonic demand is arriving before profit
insights.summary: AAOI quarterly revenue rose from $118.6M to $191.9M across the four stored periods, but the latest operating loss widened to $24.7M. This confirms demand acceleration while arguing against treating revenue momentum as operating leverage.

insights.title: Power may reprice before software
insights.summary: The same AI demand signal touches neocloud capacity, grid scarcity, and optical interconnects. The less crowded expression may sit one layer below compute revenue.

insights.title: Quantum growth is not yet operating leverage
insights.summary: IONQ revenue rose from $39.9M to $80.0M across the stored quarters, while operating loss widened from $168.8M to $337.2M. Fast top-line growth currently strengthens rather than falsifies the bearish fundamentals-gap thesis.

insights.title: AI power is a maturity barbell
insights.summary: The same power thesis contains very different underwriting objects: GEV reported $11.1B of Q2 revenue and $653M of operating income, while OKLO reported $1.2M of revenue and a $73.2M operating loss. Treat operating infrastructure and pre-commercial optionality as separate risk sleeves.

insights.title: Trade the event graph, not the IPO
insights.summary: Nscale may be untradeable directly, but its filing window can still reprice public neocloud and power comps. The event is useful even if participation is skipped.

insights.title: Narrative baskets compete for the same risk budget
insights.summary: Quantum momentum can weaken when capital rotates toward infrastructure names with visible contracts and utilization.

relations.rationale: Compute expansion depends on available power, interconnects, and grid timing.
GPU clusters pull networking and optical demand forward.
Both express different layers of the same data-center build cycle.
Both attract speculative capital, but only one currently has visible utilization economics.

events.label: Nscale possible U.S. IPO
events.summary: Nscale potential U.S. IPO as soon as September 2026; reports cite up to $3B raise, $51B contracted revenue, Anyscale acquisition, and large power/data-center commitments. Not confirmed for Aug 24 and not currently Robinhood-tradable.
events.rationale: No direct participation before a confirmed filing, terms, ticker, and Robinhood tradability. Use the event to monitor public comps.
events.participation_trigger: Reassess after filing terms are public and liquidity can be evaluated.

cycles.hypothesis: AI power beneficiaries sustain relative strength through the next capex-guidance cycle.
cycles.preregistered_outcome: Basket outperforms software AI proxies with improving breadth and no drawdown beyond the hard risk limit.

cycles.thesis_name: Neocloud and GPU compute burst basket
cycles.hypothesis: A confirmed Nscale filing expands volatility and attention across listed neocloud comps.
cycles.preregistered_outcome: At least two public comps show volume expansion around the filing window without a financing-quality break.

cycles.thesis_name: AI semiconductor and photonics second derivative
cycles.hypothesis: Optical suppliers capture a second derivative of cluster capex.
cycles.preregistered_outcome: Two suppliers improve demand commentary before year-end and the basket holds after doubled-cost stress.

cycles.hypothesis: Quantum momentum fades relative to infrastructure when speculative liquidity contracts.
cycles.preregistered_outcome: Quantum basket underperforms neoclouds in the next risk-off rotation.

tests.autopsy: The signal only survived high-liquidity momentum regimes and repeated a previously observed failure.
Leverage amplified correlated financing risk; the expression duplicated one underlying factor.
Volume confirmation improved results; financing screens prevented the worst tail outcomes.
Entry sensitivity overfit the recent momentum regime and failed during rate-volatility expansion.
Held positive expectancy after doubled costs; drawdown remained inside the hard limit.

agent_runs.summary: Matched the failure to a prior speculative-liquidity regime dependency.
Flagged repeated underweighting of financing risk in high-beta infrastructure expressions.
Replayed the thesis at doubled transaction costs and in the 2022 rates shock.
Independent source agents found power, fuel, and grid bottleneck evidence without current-price context.

lessons.summary: Quantum breakout signals have not survived outside high-liquidity speculative regimes.
Levered neocloud baskets conceal a shared financing factor; exposure must be capped at the factor level.
Fast-entry variants overfit recent power momentum and breach drawdown limits during rate shocks.
